mission: Ben arrives on Coruscant roughly half a day after Elya sent the message. The body is not warm-on-the-floor fresh, but the investigation is fresh: access controlled, first reports unfinished, official assumptions still forming. Inspector Cale Dorrin, a GA Justice / Coruscant Security investigator assigned to sensitive old-GAG and political-crime cases, controls the scene and lets Ben in under limits because Elya’s message makes him relevant and Luke has quietly vouched for the urgency. Ben senses Force-trauma and recovers the damaged Jacen-sealed duplicate manifest fragment hidden by Elya’s records instincts, not in an obvious safe.
why_now: The fragment is not enough to solve the case. It shows a duplicated shipment identity, a quarantine/survey disguise, Jacen’s personal encryption marker, and a partial GAG logistics/audit trace. Dorrin can validate the official case context and preserve access, but he cannot interpret what the fragment means.
conflict: The fragment is not enough to solve the case. turning_point: Dorrin’s first records check points toward an old GAG personnel/prosecution trail Ben cannot interpret alone.
closing_hook: Dorrin’s first records check points toward an old GAG personnel/prosecution trail Ben cannot interpret alone.
setting: Coruscant, the third-floor records office at the Coruscant Bureau of Post-Conflict Logistics — roughly twelve hours after Elya's death. GA Justice has secured the scene; Inspector Cale Dorrin controls access. Elya's body has been removed but the chair, terminal, and blood smear on the terminal edge remain. Daytime overhead lighting now, harsh and fluorescent. Other Bureau offices on the floor have been cleared for the investigation.
